entries.reason: the release does not carry it at all: read from 6.1.3's own MediaPlayer with tools/mach32_methods.py, the getter hasProtectedAsset is in none of the 236 classes' own instance lists and in none of the 41 categories - not on MPMediaItem (75 own methods), not on MPMediaEntity (18), not on MPConcreteMediaItem (29). The accessors it is a convenience over are present: valueForProperty: is an own method of MPMediaEntity at 6.1.3. The header declares it as the property protectedAsset with getter = hasProtectedAsset, so the property name is not a selector and the getter is what is implemented.
entries.effect: a port-created item answers hasProtectedAsset from its own property dictionary under the key 'hasProtectedAsset'; a real item is answered by the release, whose concrete class implements nothing here, and a subclass's own method always wins over a category on its public ancestor
entries.key_measured: measured, not a convention: the value of the MPMediaItemProperty* constant of that name on this Mac's own MediaPlayer. The rule it gives is the property's own name except where the 26.2 header declares a getter=, where it is the getter's name - and the constants 6.1.3 already had show it, IsCompilation being isCompilation and IsCloudItem isCloudItem
entries.key_measurement: tests/backports/host/mediaplayeritem/constant-values.m, compiled with xcrun clang -fobjc-arc -framework Foundation -framework MediaPlayer and run: it reads the constants and nothing else, no library and no query, output committed at tests/backports/host/mediaplayeritem/evidence/constant-values.txt
entries.key_unverified: what is still unverified is that a **populated** item answers this getter with that value, which needs a media library: neither this Mac nor 6.1.3 can be given a populated MPMediaItem. See coordination/crutches.md
